newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus to sell more T-bills, issue foreign bonds.
newsitem.headline: Belarus to sell more T-bills, issue foreign bonds.

text.p: The Belarussian central bank plans to increase Treasury bill (GKO) issues and issue securities denominated in hard currencies next year, a senior bank official said on Monday.

"Issuing hard-currency denominated securities, and entering the world financial market, will raise Belarus's rating in the eyes of foreign investors," securities department chief Rodion Tikhonov told reporters.
He said Belarus had issued 5.5 trillion roubles in short-term Treasury bills as of November 1 this year, compared to 525.7 billion roubles at the same time last year.
"This year we achieved a breakthrough on the T-bill market and we plan to increase volumes next year," Tikhonov said.
Belarus, which began selling T-bills in 1994, now issues them in three- and six-month maturities.
The government plans to cover 53 percent, or 4.1 trillion roubles, of the 1997 budget deficit with T-bill sales, he said.
"We intend to continue increasing the maturities of the T-bills, and in 1997 move into releasing long-term bills."
The first issue of long-term T-bills (DGOs) would be 30 billion roubles, and the maturity term would be set by the central bank, he added.
